title: Twisting modules and degree-generated opens on glued relative Proj
statement: Let $Z$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal B=\bigoplus_{j\geq0}\mathcal B_j$ a commutative unital graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures] with each degree quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $\pi:Y=\operatorname{Proj}_Z(\mathcal B)\to Z$ be the glued relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj]. There are quasi-coherent modules $E_j$ on $Y$ for $j\in\mathbf Z$, with $E_0=\mathcal O_Y$, a commutative unital graded multiplication $E_i\otimes E_j\to E_{i+j}$, and a canonical graded map $\eta:\pi^*\mathcal B\to\bigoplus_{j\geq0}E_j$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. On every affine $V\subseteq Z$, with $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal B)$, these data identify with the twisting modules $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Proj}(A)}(j)$, their multiplication and their canonical homogeneous-section map [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. The identifications commute with all further affine base restrictions and their cocycles, and determine the data up to unique isomorphism respecting these identifications. For every $d\geq1$ the open subsets $\bigcup_{a\in A_d}D_+(a)$ in these affine-base models agree on overlaps and define an open $Y_d\subseteq Y$. On $Y_d$ the module $E_d$ is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], multiplication gives $E_d^{\otimes k}|_{Y_d}\simeq E_{kd}|_{Y_d}$ for all $k\geq0$, and $\eta_d:\pi^*\mathcal B_d|_{Y_d}\to E_d|_{Y_d}$ is surjective. We have $Y=\bigcup_{d\geq1}Y_d$ and $Y_d\subseteq Y_{ad}$ for every $a\geq1$. On $Y_d$, the universal degree-$ad$ data are the $a$th tensor power and Veronese restriction of the universal degree-$d$ data, under the multiplication isomorphisms. No equality $\mathcal B_0=\mathcal O_Z$ or finite generation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01NR (lemma-glue-relative-proj-twists), Tag 01MS (lemma-when-invertible), equation-Ud before Tag 01N8, and the open-immersion comparison in Tag 01NY (lemma-relative-proj).

proof.text: For affine $W\subseteq V\subseteq Z$, put $R=\mathcal O_Z(V)$, $S=\mathcal O_Z(W)$ and $A=\bigoplus_j\mathcal B_j(V)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-affine-section-base-change] to each $\mathcal B_j$: the maps $S\otimes_R A_j\to\mathcal B_j(W)$, $s\otimes a\mapsto s(a|_W)$, are isomorphisms. Their direct sum $\beta:S\otimes_RA\to\mathcal B(W)$ is a graded $S$-algebra isomorphism, since restriction respects unit and products, and $\psi(a)=\beta(1\otimes a)=a|_W$ is the graded restriction map. Thus [lem-sfb-proj-scalar-extension-twist-comparison], applied to $R\to S$, $A$, $B=\mathcal B(W)$ and $\beta$, gives isomorphisms from the restricted twist over $V$ to the twist over $W$, preserving homogeneous sections and multiplication. Their underlying scheme maps are those of [lem-nagata-proj-affine-restriction]. For affine $W'\subseteq W\subseteq V$ the isomorphism for $W'\subseteq V$ is the composite of those for $W\subseteq V$ and $W'\subseteq W$, since restriction maps compose. The identity and composition assertions of the twist comparison give the identity and cocycle equations for a chain of affine inclusions.

For two affine base opens $V,V'$, cover $V\cap V'$ by affine opens $W$. On $\pi^{-1}W$ compare the two twists via the twist over $W$ from step 1. On intersections of two such $W$, refine again by affine opens: transitivity in step 1 says that both comparisons are the same. By the morphism-gluing clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules], the comparisons glue on $\pi^{-1}(V\cap V')$. The same calculation on affine refinements gives their triple-overlap cocycle. Its clause (2) now glues the twists degree by degree to modules $E_j$ on $Y$. Each affine-model twist is quasi-coherent by clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists], applied to $M=A(j)$. Every point of $Y$ has an affine neighborhood inside one such model with the required module presentation; hence each $E_j$ is quasi-coherent by [pqf-def-coherent]. No base intersection was assumed affine.

source.place: Tag 01NR (lemma-glue-relative-proj-twists), first paragraph of proof; relative-glueing-sheaves, affine refinement of overlaps

proof.text: On $D_+(f)\subseteq\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ use multiplication of localized fractions $(a/f^m,b/f^n)\mapsto ab/f^{m+n}$. It is bilinear and commutes with restriction, because the restriction maps in [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] are localization homomorphisms. It therefore defines a bilinear sheaf map. The universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] produces the multiplication morphisms between twists. Step 1 makes these compatible on affine base restrictions, and [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] (1) glues them to $E_i\otimes E_j\to E_{i+j}$. The unit and associative and commutative identities hold on fractions, hence on the standard-open cover and then on $Y$. Since $(A_f)_0$ is the structure ring on each standard open, the same gluing identifies $E_0$ with $\mathcal O_Y$.

source.place: Tag 01MK (lemma-widetilde-tensor), its bilinear construction; equations 01MO and 01MP; Tag 01NR

proof.text: For $j\geq0$, send $a\in\mathcal B_j(V)$ to the section $a/1$ of the affine-model twist, using [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (3). Step 1 identifies its restriction with $(a|_W)/1$. These maps on the affine basis define a sheaf morphism $\mathcal B_j\to\pi_*E_j$; on arbitrary opens it sends a section to the unique glued image of its affine restrictions. Transpose by the pullback adjunction in [def-pc-module-pullback] to obtain $\eta_j:\pi^*\mathcal B_j\to E_j$. The fraction identities $(ab)/1=(a/1)(b/1)$ and $1/1=1$ show that the maps assemble to a unital graded algebra map $\eta$. For two glued systems with the prescribed affine identifications, compose one affine identification with the inverse of the other. These isomorphisms agree on overlaps by step 1, so [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] (1) glues them and their inverses uniquely. They respect $\eta$ and multiplication locally and hence globally. This proves the asserted normalized uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 01NR (lemma-glue-relative-proj-twists), homogeneous-section map, functorial gluing, and uniqueness

proof.text: Fix $d\geq1$. In the notation of step 1, $\mathcal B_d(W)=S\otimes_R A_d$. The inverse image of $D_+(a)$ under the restriction map is $D_+(\bar a)$ by [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension]. Every element $b$ of $\mathcal B_d(W)$ is a finite sum $\sum_i s_i\bar a_i$, $a_i\in A_d$. If $b$ is outside a homogeneous prime $\mathfrak q$, then some $\bar a_i$ is outside $\mathfrak q$, since $\mathfrak q$ is an ideal. Conversely each $\bar a_i$ is a degree-$d$ element. Thus $\bigcup_{b\in\mathcal B_d(W)}D_+(b)$ equals the inverse image of $\bigcup_{a\in A_d}D_+(a)$. On overlaps refine by affine opens as in step 2; these equalities glue the prescribed opens to $Y_d\subseteq Y$.

source.place: Equation 01N5 (equation-Ud); Tag 01NY (lemma-relative-proj), affine restriction of degree opens

proof.text: On a chart $D_+(f)$ with $f\in A_d$, multiplication by $f$ identifies $(A_f)_0$ with $(A_f)_d$; its inverse is multiplication by $f^{-1}$. These formulas also commute with localization to smaller opens, so they trivialize $E_d$ there by [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. Thus $E_d|_{Y_d}$ is invertible by [def-sc-invertible-module]. For $k\geq0$, the iterated multiplication map sends the tensor of $k$ copies of the frame $f$ to $f^k$, a frame for $(A_f)_{kd}$, so it is an isomorphism on this cover. For $k=0$ this is $E_0=\mathcal O_Y$. Finally $\eta_d$ sends the pulled section $f$ to that frame; every germ of the target is a scalar multiple of it, which proves surjectivity. These local inverses agree wherever both are defined, since they invert the same multiplication map, and therefore give the stated global isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 01MS (lemma-when-invertible), explicit inverse after inverting f; equation 01N5 and the paragraph following 01N6

proof.text: Every point of $\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ is a homogeneous prime not containing $A_+$, so some homogeneous $f$ of positive degree is outside it. Hence the $Y_d$ cover $Y$. If $f\in A_d$ and $a\geq1$, primality gives $f\notin\mathfrak p$ if and only if $f^a\notin\mathfrak p$; consequently $D_+(f)=D_+(f^a)\subseteq Y_{ad}$ and $Y_d\subseteq Y_{ad}$. On $D_+(f)$ the isomorphism $E_d^{\otimes a}\simeq E_{ad}$ is $f^{\otimes a}\mapsto f^a$. In Veronese degree $n$, both the degree-$ad$ section map and the restriction of the degree-$d$ map send $b\in A_{adn}$ to the same fraction $b/1$. Their coefficient in the frame $f^{an}$ is $b/f^{an}$. Thus the universal data on $Y_d$ agree in every degree, including degree zero, with the $a$th tensor power and Veronese restriction. These equalities persist under base restriction by step 1. The whole construction used arbitrary quasi-coherent degrees; neither finite generation nor $\mathcal B_0=\mathcal O_Z$ entered.
